narrative.northStar: Engineer's Editorial — a deep-void typographic site with one committed flame of orange.
narrative.overview: The site reads as a senior platform engineer's personal newsroom. The page is a deep, almost-black void (#050505) softened by a barely-visible 64px grid, an asymmetric vignette, and an 1.8%-opacity noise grain. Long-form typography carries the work: Clash Display sets the headlines with confident geometric authority, DM Sans sets the body in a light weight at long line-heights so technical posts read like printed essays, and JetBrains Mono handles every label, timestamp, tag, and metadata pill. One committed orange (#ff6b00) carries identity wherever it lands. The aesthetic is editorial-typographic with a bold technical edge, not terminal-cosplay or SaaS-marketing. The dark surface is committed (Drenched-tier) but the accent stays Restrained-tier (≤10%). That tension — drenched darkness, rationed warmth — is the brand: bold without shouting, technical without cosplay.
keyCharacteristics: Drenched dark surface (#050505) with rationed orange accent (#ff6b00)
Three-font stack: Clash Display (display), DM Sans (light editorial body), JetBrains Mono (engineering labels)
Long body line-heights (1.6 base, 1.9 in prose) with a min(80ch, 100%) reading column
Generous radii: pills for chrome (nav, CTA, badges), 24px on content cards, 12px on images and code
Atmosphere layers: 64px grid + radial vignette + 1.8%-opacity SVG noise + ambient orange hero glow
Motion is breath, not choreography: 0.8s reveal-up, 6s glow breathe, exponential cubic-bezier easing

rules.name: The One Flame Rule
rules.body: The accent (#ff6b00) is rationed. On any screen, it appears in at most a handful of places: one CTA, the link underlines, list markers, the typed-out role, the timeline dot. If the page starts to read as 'orange', remove uses until it reads as 'dark with one warm point of attention'.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Black Rule
rules.body: The body uses #050505, not #000. Text uses #f2f2f0, not #fff. Every neutral carries a single drop of warmth toward the brand hue.

rules.name: The Drenched-Surface, Restrained-Accent Rule
rules.body: The dark is Drenched (the surface IS the color, full bleed, no respite). The orange is Restrained (≤10%). The contrast is the brand.

rules.name: The Mono-Metadata Rule
rules.body: Every piece of metadata — date, read time, tag, badge, table header, ordered-list numeral, code-frame filename — is set in JetBrains Mono. Body prose is never mono.

rules.name: The Light-Body Rule
rules.body: Body copy uses DM Sans weight 300, not the default 400. Pair this with line-height 1.9 in prose; never tighten below 1.6.

rules.name: The Accent-Underlined-Link Rule
rules.body: Every body link uses border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-accent) with text-decoration: none. On hover, the link's text color shifts to accent, the underline disappears, and a 4px-padded accent-dim background pill appears around the word.

rules.name: The No-Material-Shadow Rule
rules.body: This is not a Material-style elevation system. Depth comes from translucent fills, backdrop-blur, and the layered atmosphere stack. Box-shadow is reserved for glows and embedded-artifact drops.

rules.name: The Atmosphere Stack Rule
rules.body: Every page composes the same four fixed-position background layers: .grid-bg + body void + .vignette + .noise-overlay. Don't bypass this stack on a per-page basis.

rules.name: The Pill-Chrome, Slab-Content Rule
rules.body: Chrome elements (nav, CTA, badges, tags) are full pills or near-pills. Content surfaces (blog cards) are large 24px slabs. The contrast is the visual rhythm.

rules.name: The Backdrop-Blur Floats Rule
rules.body: Glass (translucent + backdrop-blur) is reserved for elements that genuinely float above content: the nav capsule, the blog card surface. Don't use glass decoratively as a default.

dos: Do start every page from the four-layer atmosphere stack: .grid-bg + body #050505 + .vignette + .noise-overlay.
Do rate-limit #ff6b00 to ≤10% of any screen — the One Flame Rule. If the page reads as 'orange', remove uses.
Do set every piece of metadata (dates, tags, badges, table headers, code-frame filenames, ordered-list numerals) in JetBrains Mono, with letter-spacing 0.02em to 0.06em.
Do keep body copy in DM Sans weight 300 with line-height ≥ 1.6 (1.9 in prose).
Do use the accent-underlined link pattern (border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-accent), text-decoration: none) on every body link.
Do preserve the accent-bar underline (60px × 2px with glow) under every prose H2.
Do use ease-out-quint (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for reveal and timeline transitions.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion — the existing media query disables reveals, glow breathing, and timeline transitions.
donts: Don't use pure #000 for backgrounds or pure #fff for text. Body sits at #050505, text at #f2f2f0.
Don't introduce side-stripe colored borders (border-left ≥ 2px in an accent color) on cards, list items, or arbitrary callouts. The blockquote and GitHub alerts are documented exceptions.
Don't ship gradient text (background-clip: text on a gradient). The accent is a solid color.
Don't build a generic SaaS gradient hero — no purple-to-blue, no hero-metric template, no identical-card grids.
Don't drop the system back into a Medium/Substack default — no default serif on white, no stock 'min read' chrome.
Don't edge toward crypto/neon-on-black — no neon greens or pinks, no glitch, no scanlines.
Don't add corporate-consulting trust signals — no navy + gold, no stock photography, no 'Solutions / Capabilities / Insights' IA.
Don't use Material-style box-shadow elevation. Depth is layered atmosphere + translucent fills + backdrop-blur.
Don't use em dashes in body copy or UI text. Use commas, colons, semicolons, periods, or parentheses.
Don't add new fonts. The three-font stack — Clash Display / DM Sans / JetBrains Mono — is the brand.
Don't wrap content surfaces in .glass-panel decoratively. Glass is reserved for elements that genuinely float.
